evidence: src/infrastructure/OrderController.ts: placeOrder, updateOrderState, cancelOrder and listByState each repeat `catch (error) { const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'; res.status(400).json({ error: message }); }`
src/infrastructure/ProductController.ts: getStockLevels repeats the same catch block that maps errors to a 400 response

src/infrastructure/OrderController.ts: updateOrderState checks `typeof stateValue !== 'string' && !Array.isArray(stateValue)`, while listByState checks `!stateValue || (typeof stateValue !== 'string' && !Array.isArray(stateValue))`. The two checks differ, so validation of the state input is duplicated and inconsistent
src/infrastructure/app.ts: `function initializeProducts(productRepository: InMemoryProductRepository)` depends on the concrete class instead of the ProductRepository interface
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module groups infrastructure adapters: in-memory repositories, Express controllers and the composition root in app.ts. Keeping these in one folder is normal for a small hexagonal app. The failure is that one rule lives in five places. Mapping any thrown error to HTTP 400 with { error: message } is copied into five handlers across OrderController.ts and ProductController.ts instead of sitting in one shared helper or middleware. Validation of the order-state input is also written twice in OrderController.ts with different checks: updateOrderState doesn't reject an empty string but listByState does, and both accept arrays even though updateOrderState's message says 'must be a string'. A minor point: initializeProducts in app.ts takes the concrete InMemoryProductRepository instead of the ProductRepository interface used in the rest of the wiring.

violations.message: The rule that maps errors to HTTP 400 is copied into all four handlers (placeOrder, updateOrderState, cancelOrder, listByState) instead of living in one place. State-input validation is also duplicated: updateOrderState and listByState check differently (only listByState rejects an empty string).
getStockLevels repeats the same error-to-400 catch block as OrderController, so the HTTP error policy is copied across controllers.
initializeProducts takes the concrete InMemoryProductRepository instead of the ProductRepository interface, bypassing the abstraction used in the rest of the wiring.
